title: Sprint-bucketized price sensitivity and hire priorities (Apr 15 2026)
content:
Purpose:
Quick, operational-friendly budgeting sheet to decide which hires to pull into the next 8-week feature window and how slab / per-token pricing changes materially affect hire needs and runway. Working doc — contains assumptions, three sensitivity scenarios, and a sprint-bucketized hire schedule plus near-term mitigations.

One-line summary:
If price realization drops by 12% vs plan we need to delay 1 backend hire and convert 2 FTEs to contractors (8-week window) to preserve a 24-week runway cushion. If price increases +10% we can pull forward one SRE and keep all hires.

Assumptions (explicit):
- Baseline ARR velocity: $1.2M net new annualized from current pipeline across hosted API and Dedicated contracts.
- April token mix (weighted avg unit): 0.00018 USD/token (Baseline price used for revenue estimation).
- Variable cost per token (infra + amortized GPU): $0.00007/token.
- Fixed G&A and R&D burn baseline: $1.1M/month (excludes incremental hires in this plan).
- Average fully-burdened monthly cost per new hire (engineer) = $18.5k, product/PM = $15k, SRE = $20k, solutions engineer = $16k.
- Hiring lead time in weeks: 6 (expected ramp to full productiveness in 12 weeks).
- This sheet models an 8-week feature window (two 4-week sprints).

Scenario matrix (sensitivity to realized price relative to baseline):
Columns: Scenario | Price vs baseline | Revenue delta (8w est) | Available budget delta (8w) | Headcount action
Base | 0% | $0 | $0 | Hire as planned (3 eng, 1 prod, 1 se)
Down -12% | -12% | -$96k | -$96k | Delay 1 backend hire, convert 2 hires to 8-week contractors (~$60k savings), postpone SRE
Up +10% | +10% | +$80k | +$80k | Pull forward SRE, keep planned hires + add small trial contractor for perf testing

Quick math notes:
- 8-week revenue impact approximated as (base monthly revenue * 2) * price delta. Base monthly revenue used here = $400k (simplified estimate from ARR velocity and current bookings cadence).
- Budget delta available used to offset incremental headcount and contractor costs in the period.

Sprint-bucketized hire schedule (8-week window):
Sprint 1 (weeks 1–4):
- Backend eng (1) — start 
- Backend eng (1) — start (if base or up scenario)
- Product manager (1) — start
- Solutions engineer (1) — start (customer pilot)
Sprint 2 (weeks 5–8):
- SRE (1) — start (only in base/up)
- Perf contractor (0.5 FTE equivalent) — start (if up)

Budget snippet (monthlyized representation for clarity):
Month | Fixed burn (baseline) | Incremental hires cost (month) | Total burn | Notes
Apr (partial 8w) | $1,100,000 | $55,500 | $1,155,500 | baseline + 3 hires starting mid-month (prorated)
May | $1,100,000 | $111,000 | $1,211,000 | full month of incremental hires

Column meanings: incremental hires cost = sum(fully-burdened monthly) * prorate factor for hires ramping. Example: 3 eng * $18.5k = $55.5k/month.

Cost/benefit tradeoffs explored: 
- Contractor vs hire: we modeled replacing 1 backend hire with contractors at 1.3x hourly cost but no severance/benefits and 0.6 productivity in month 2 — net short-term savings ~ $20k per 8-week window but reduces long-term velocity.
- SRE deferral saves $20k/month but risks latency SLOs for new routes — insurance cost measured as potential $40k churn risk (customer credits + support + ops).
- Small perf contractor (0.5 FTE) accelerates quantization rollout and could reduce variable cost/token by ~3–4% long term (savings hard to capture in 8-week window).

Mini sensitivity table (numbers illustrative):
Metric | Base | Price -12% | Price +10%
8-week revenue (est) | $800,000 | $704,000 | $880,000
Variable cost (8w) | $312,000 | $312,000 | $312,000
Gross margin (8w) | $488,000 | $392,000 | $568,000
Incremental hires cost (8w) | $111,000 | $70,000 | $111,000
Net delta vs base | $0 | -$96,000 | +$80,000

Proposed near-term mitigations (if price softness observed within first 2 weeks):
- Pause non-critical procurement (license renewals flagged) — target savings $18k in 8w.
- Freeze non-customer-facing hiring (UX/Design) — reallocate $30k.
- Convert two backend new-hire offers to contractor engagements (60 day trial) — estimated 8w saving $60k as above.
- Trigger alert to sales: push higher-yield enterprise pilots with custom SLAs to raise realized price (list of accounts: ACCT-101, ACCT-124).

Open questions / data fetch required:
- Confirm actual realized token price by customer cohort for last 12 weeks (ask billing analytics, ethan@) — needed to upgrade estimates from heuristic to booked reality.
- Get updated recruiting pipeline and earliest start dates for the 3 prioritized backend candidates (Ravi recruiting).
- Estimate churn head risk if SRE is deferred (SLO alert cost modeling from SRE team).

Action items (owner clear):
- Ethan: pull token realization by cohort (due 2026-04-20)
- Ravi: confirm candidate start-date windows and contractor rates (due 2026-04-22)
- Sofia: update this sheet with final booked revenue numbers and re-run sensitivity (due 2026-04-24)

Notes to reviewers (informal):
- This is intentionally conservative on expected immediate cost savings from quantization — upstream infra team says measurable savings kick in after 12–16 weeks of production traffic; our 8-week window will mostly capture hiring & procurement levers.
- If we see mixed signals (some grouplogic customers up, small customers down), prefer converting 1 hire to contractor rather than delaying SRE unless SLO risk materializes.
